title: Smooth null screen and KN parameter family

items.title: Smooth null screen and subextremal Kerr–Newman parameter family
items.statement: Let $(\mathcal M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with the metric-selected connection $\nabla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Here $N$ is the supplied smooth future timelike vector field defining the time orientation; it is not a coordinate frame or a tetrad.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), complete 238-page lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 7, equations (7.114)–(7.128), printed pp. 207–214 (PDF pp. 213–220), for the Kerr parameter family, horizons and generator context.

references.title: Tim Adamo and E. T. Newman, The Kerr-Newman Metric: A Review, arXiv:1410.6626v2
references.locator: Section 3.3, equations (3.18)–(3.21), printed pp. 16–17 (PDF pp. 17–18), for the KN root and advanced-coordinate horizon data.

references.locator: Chapter 7, the null tetrad and its normalized null pair in equations (7.121)–(7.123), printed pp. 208–209 (PDF pp. 214–215); the local proof supplies the quotient argument.

items.title: Verified Kerr-Newman family first law and Smarr identity
items.statement: On the strictly subextremal open parameter family $\mathcal P$ of [[def-tgr-horizon-screen-family]], use the outer-horizon functions $(r_+,D,A,j,\kappa_{\rm KN},\Omega_{\rm KN},\Phi_{\rm KN})$ defined there. These functions give the exact selected-model outer-horizon data throughout $\mathcal P$: [[prop-emg-xs-kn-horizon-data]] verifies every point with $a^2+q^2>0$, and [[lem-tgr-schwarzschild-horizon-data]] verifies the remaining point $a=q=0$. title: Smooth null screen and KN parameter family — Examples

items.title: Schwarzschild and charged endpoint algebra
items.statement: Take the nonrotating slice $a=0$ of the parameter family in [[def-tgr-horizon-screen-family]].

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), complete 238-page lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 7, equations (7.114)–(7.155), printed pp. 207–215 (PDF pp. 213–221), for Kerr/Schwarzschild family parameters, area and surface-gravity context; the charged endpoint is checked from the exact local supplier.

references.title: Tim Adamo and E. T. Newman, The Kerr-Newman Metric: A Review, arXiv:1410.6626v2
references.locator: Section 3.3, equations (3.18)–(3.21), and Section 4 equations (4.1)–(4.2), printed pp. 16–21 (PDF pp. 17–22), for charged horizons, area and family work terms.

references.title: Robert M. Wald, The Thermodynamics of Black Holes, Living Reviews in Relativity 4 (2001), 6
references.locator: Section 2, PDF pp. 6–8, on stationary first-law scope; its global hypotheses are not used for this algebraic example.

items.title: Flat focusing cone without future smooth completeness
items.statement: The claim that $\operatorname{Ric}(k,k)\ge0$ alone forces the area of every smooth compact cross-section of every future null congruence to be nondecreasing, even when its smooth affine description ends at a finite future parameter, is false.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), complete 238-page lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 7, equations (7.148)–(7.156), printed pp. 215–216 (PDF pp. 221–222), for the Kerr area-law and classical-mechanics context; the cone calculation is local.

references.title: Robert M. Wald, The Thermodynamics of Black Holes, Living Reviews in Relativity 4 (2001), 6
references.locator: Section 2, PDF pp. 3–5, for focusing under null convergence and the need for future extension/global horizon hypotheses.

references.title: Tim Adamo and E. T. Newman, The Kerr-Newman Metric: A Review, arXiv:1410.6626v2
references.locator: Section 3.3, equations (3.18)–(3.21), for explicit null horizon-generator context; no KN calculation is used in this flat counterexample.
